children: The reported cuts would come on top of 9,000 previously planned reductions as Porsche grapples with cost pressures and weakening demand

Porsche could cut a further 4,000 jobs as part of Volkswagen Group’s restructuring drive, according to German business daily Handelsblatt. The reported plan would add to previously agreed workforce reductions at the luxury carmaker.

Porsche management and labour representatives had earlier agreed to eliminate around 9,000 jobs, including 4,000 cuts announced previously and a further 5,000 agreed in July. The latest proposal could take the total number of planned reductions to around 13,000, with the earlier measures expected to be implemented by 2035.

The additional cuts are reportedly aimed at addressing an estimated €700 million shortfall in overhead savings. Volkswagen’s supervisory board has reportedly documented approval for the latest restructuring proposal, although the parent company cannot directly enforce the measures at Porsche.

The potential reductions come as Porsche faces declining sales in China, US tariffs and setbacks in its electric vehicle strategy. Volkswagen recently lowered its 2026 operating margin outlook to around 1 per cent, citing significant one-off costs, including a major writedown linked to Porsche.
Neither Volkswagen nor Porsche commented on the newly reported job cuts. The number of positions affected, timing and implementation details have not been officially confirmed.
